title: Queue-based human gate for squash-merge commit provenance repair
context: Squash-merges produce a new commit whose parent is the pre-merge tip, orphaning the original per-commit SHAs that decision provenance links cite. These orphaned links need repair, but matching orphaned decisions to newly-merged commits via file-set overlap is not reliable enough to trust an unattended write into shared team memory. Touches invariant(s): con_7217ab24ab (Regression guard: "Flaky test failure under parallelism: native tree-sitter module resolution race on Windows" must not recur.); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Implement a human-gatekeeping queue system for commit provenance repair. Orphaned decisions are matched to merged commits based on file-set overlap, queued in `.hunch/pending-commit-repairs.json`, and require explicit `--apply` approval. Rejected matches are durably tombstoned in `.hunch/dropped-commit-repairs.json` to prevent re-queuing identical rejections. Repairs surface as escalations prompting human confirmation.
consequences: Shared team memory is never auto-modified in response to squash-merges; all repairs require explicit human confirmation
Introduces new queue files and CLI commands (`--apply`, `--drop`) to manage repairs
Requires robust handling of corrupted queue files: duplicate-id entries keyed by object identity, withhold-not-drop semantics for unresolvable commits, non-actionable entries marked transparently
Post-merge hook opportunistically detects orphaning and queues repairs, surfacing them as inline escalations
Durable tombstones prevent resurrection of previously rejected matches across multiple detection runs
alternatives_rejected: Automatic repair without human approval — file-set overlap matching is insufficient to trust an unattended write into shared team memory
Using git's rename detection as the match signal — too weak for this use case
Volatile queue clearing on `--drop` — durable tombstones required to prevent re-queuing of identical rejections
